record.original_question: Does every closed Riemannian manifold contain a closed geodesic multinet that does not contain any non-trivial periodic geodesic? Here "closed" means there are no unbalanced (boundary) vertices, and a geodesic multinet is the version of a geodesic net that allows edge multiplicities and self-intersections.

evidence.quote: Problem 2.0.1. Is it true that each closed Riemannian manifold contains a closed geodesic multinet not containing a non-trivial periodic geodesic?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a closed (compact, without boundary) Riemannian manifold. A geodesic net in $M$ is a finite graph immersed in $M$ whose edges are geodesic arcs and which satisfies a balancing condition at each vertex: at every vertex $v$, the sum of the unit tangent vectors of the edges emanating from $v$, counted with edge multiplicities, equals the zero vector in $T_v M$. A geodesic multinet is a geodesic net in which edges are allowed to have positive integer multiplicities and edges are allowed to self-intersect or coincide. Such a multinet is called closed if every vertex satisfies the balancing condition (i.e. there are no unbalanced "boundary" vertices). A non-trivial periodic geodesic is a closed geodesic that is not a constant map.

Question: Does every closed Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ contain a closed geodesic multinet that does not contain any non-trivial periodic geodesic as a subset (i.e., none of the geodesic arcs traced by the multinet, with their multiplicities, decompose to include a non-trivial closed geodesic)?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem in the literature on geodesic nets and multinets. A targeted web search did not return any subsequent work announcing a resolution, and standard references on closed geodesics do not address this specific question about geodesic multinets. The status appears to remain open.
